title: Draftsman #341 Plan C: listener docs and skills, and listener-aware diagrams and browser
outcome: Dale's Draftsman explains, in its docs and in the skills agents load, exactly how to find or create the listener a call lands on without duplicates or guesses. The diagrams and the browser then show those listeners: each call enters the listener it names in the Application view, the Deployment view prints that listener's port, and the browser lists a Listener for every connection and the listeners each component owns.

epics.title: Listener docs and skills: lookup-before-create
acceptance_criteria: The Draftsman docs describe the listener object and the lookup-before-create procedure #341 specifies: resolve the owner, normalize the identity key (owner + protocol + port + endpoint; lowercase protocol, default ports filled in, host dropped, path parameters templated), then link an exact match silently or create a stub listener (catalogStatus: stub) and link it; an ambiguous owner or key is listed and asked, never guessed; a later authored listener upgrades the stub in place; a vendor-owned stub needs a company-internal relationship owner before it leaves stub; the SDP completeness gate blocks calls to internally owned stubs. object-types, how-to-add-objects, draftsman and relationship docs say every relationship names a targetListener. A docs test pins the procedure's key statements and the release note is added.

The Draftsman skills (draftsman-core, draftsman-author and draftsman-query, plus the draftsman-diagram notes) carry the same lookup-before-create procedure and targetListener rule, point to the draft_table.catalog helpers (lookup_listener, create_listener_stub), and never tell an agent to guess an owner or invent a port. Skill validation, vendored-skill projection and a skills test pass, and the release note is added.

epics.title: Listener-aware renderer and browser
acceptance_criteria: Application view: a box that owns listener objects gets one attachment point per owned listener on its top edge, in a stable declared order, and a relationship with targetListener attaches to that listener's point. Boxes without listener objects keep today's per-interface entrances. Labels are unchanged and no port is shown. Output for catalogs without listener objects is byte-identical (goldens unchanged); new tests cover order, attachment and determinism.

Deployment view: a relationship's far-end technology line takes the port of the listener its targetListener names (SQL 5432, gRPC 8092), ahead of today's port resolution; through an exposed group's edge chain the hop ports still precede it (https 443 → http 8080 via <device>), and same-deployment-target traffic never takes the hop. Output for catalogs without listener objects is unchanged; tests cover the listener port, the chain and the fallback.

Browser: the Connections table gains a Listener column (the targetListener's name with protocol, port and endpoint, or blank), and a component, data component or external system detail page lists the listener objects it owns (protocol, port, endpoint, authenticationModel, catalogStatus). Existing columns stay; generated assets for the bundled examples change only by the new empty column; docs, the diagram skill and the release note are updated, and every check passes.

risks: Most of the earlier E5 renderer work already shipped for the older targetInterface design (#348-#352: per-interface entrances, port chains, the edge device chain and routing, label-overlap fix, browser exposure and Interface column). Plan only the switch to listener objects and targetListener; do not rebuild it.
No catalog in the repo has listener objects yet, so the new rendering is proven on test fixtures; output for the bundled examples must stay unchanged apart from the new browser column.
Determinism contract (D15) must hold: listener order is fixed, not file order.
